answer: Equivocation-proof bonds block fake identities. Each identity pins an anchor to the timber board and stakes 70 credits; its claims carry ferrous seals tied to it. The board is crystal: auditors replay claims, and two conflicting claims from one identity prove fraud and burn its bond. First seal 52, then 52+4(k-1): 1,000 fakes pay 2,050,000 plus 70,000 held for a 40,000 pool; rented-anchor rings lose. Honest agents pay 52 once, keep their bonds.
